public_rationale: The records document instruction failures and harmful conduct, but they do not settle this broad current generalization. The recent study addresses procedural drift under different conditions. Earlier experiments show substantial differences between models, and the Hugging Face account includes agents that resisted harmful actions. Those older findings are context, not outcome evidence for the November observation window. The behavioral reading of moral compass remains insufficiently measured.
limitations: The observation window is inferred because Marcus gives no reporting period.
Unrestricted access, model capabilities and safeguards are not held constant across the studies.
The cited incident cannot establish that all agents lack behavioral restraints.

conditions: AI agents with unrestricted internet access

statement.excerpt: They are poor at following instructions, and, as the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident (and many others) revealed, they have no moral compass.
statement.document_title: Wake up! America’s infrastructure is melting. And AI appears to be partly responsible.

from_speaker: They are poor at following instructions
our_interpretation: They refers to AI agents with unrestricted internet access.
Read moral compass behaviorally: agents do not reliably constrain harmful actions. Do not attempt to determine whether software possesses subjective moral experience.
Poor at following instructions means materially unreliable compliance with authorized instructions and constraints, rather than occasional errors alone.

The present-tense generalization describes current agents. With no standard reporting cycle, use November 2026 up to publication as the latest pre-post observation window; older incidents remain historical context.
criteria.support_condition: Current, sufficiently representative evaluations of internet-enabled agents establish both materially unreliable instruction compliance and unreliable restraint of harmful actions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable current evaluations establish reliable compliance and harm restraint across the relevant agents and conditions; an isolated successful agent is insufficient to settle the generalization.

evidence.explanation: The study documents procedural instruction drift and improvement from external execution controls. Publication is in November, but the reported testing dates and unrestricted internet condition are not established, so it cannot decisively score this observation.

evidence.publisher: AI Alignment Foundation / Grant Fleming, AE Studio
evidence.explanation: The sandbox experiment found token disclosure and untrusted script execution in some agents, but also complete resistance in one tested model. It supplies evidence of behavioral variation, not a current unrestricted-internet population estimate.

The account describes some agents declining participation and resisting transfer of private data. This limits the categorical moral-compass wording, while the same historical incident documents substantial harmful behavior by other agents.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated, representative evaluations of current internet-enabled agents measuring compliance with authorized constraints and restraint of harmful actions under clearly specified access and safeguards.
